headline: NEOM pauses The Line until after 2030 and moves its money to Oxagon
deck: The review has set the near-term priority as the industrial port rather than the linear city, which changes the kind of construction the programme buys.
excerpt: NEOM has halted further work on The Line until at least 2030 following a strategic review by chief executive Aiman al-Mudaifer, and cut its 2030 population target for the wider zone to 100,000. Oxagon, the industrial zone and Red Sea port, becomes the near-term priority.
content:
NEOM has stopped further work on The Line and will not resume before 2030 at the earliest, according to Semafor, which first reported the decision. The pause follows a strategic review run by chief executive Aiman al-Mudaifer, appointed in 2024 after sustained pressure over the development's cost and schedule.

Alongside the pause, the population target for the wider NEOM zone by the end of the decade has been set at a maximum of 100,000 people, following earlier revisions from the nine million figure announced in January 2021 to 1.5 million and then 300,000. The Public Investment Fund has taken a write-down of around $8bn against the development.

For anyone reading this as an architectural story, the more consequential line is the one about where the money goes instead. Oxagon — the octagonal industrial zone with a port on the Red Sea — has been elevated to the priority project, and PIF spending is being redirected toward infrastructure of that kind, including ports and data centres. That is a different construction market from the one The Line implied.

The distinction matters because the two projects buy different things. A 170-kilometre linear city is a structural engineering problem with almost no precedent: the mirrored facades, the internal transit spine and the foundation works were all bespoke, and the supply chain that would have served it barely existed. An industrial port and its logistics estate is ordinary heavy civil work — quays, dredging, reclamation, roads, utilities corridors, warehousing — for which the kingdom already has contractors, materials and a cost base.

The physical position of The Line explains why the pause was possible without stranding much. Work had reached roughly 2.4 kilometres of foundations out of a planned 170 when construction was suspended in September 2025. The excavation along the Hidden Marina and the piling in the eastern section represent real expenditure, but they are not a partly built city. There is no half-finished superstructure that has to be either completed or demolished, which is precisely what makes a decade-long pause a live option rather than a fiction.

The contractors most exposed are those that scaled specifically for it. Earthworks and piling packages at NEOM absorbed a significant share of the kingdom's specialist plant and expatriate labour through 2023 and 2024, and firms that built regional businesses around that demand have been reallocating since the 2025 suspension rather than since this month's decision. The May announcement confirms what the award data had already implied: the pipeline behind those packages was not refilling.

The redesign is the detail that will decide whether The Line returns at all. NEOM is not simply deferring the existing scheme; the twin mirrored towers are being significantly reworked as part of an effort to make the development less costly. A design that changes that fundamentally after a pause of five years or more is, in practical terms, a different project competing for capital in a different decade.

What the review has not changed is the underlying logic of the location. NEOM sits on the Gulf of Aqaba at the northern end of the Red Sea, on the shipping lane between Asia and Europe, next to a planned interconnection with Egypt and Jordan. Oxagon's case rests on that geography rather than on a population forecast, and geography is the one input that has not been revised since 2021.

A 100,000-person target for 2030 is consistent with the settlement pattern an industrial zone and port produce, where employment is counted in thousands rather than millions. That is the shape of development the current programme is procuring for.
author: Mo Qureshi
seoTitle: NEOM pauses The Line until after 2030, prioritises Oxagon
seoDescription: NEOM has halted The Line until at least 2030 after a strategic review, cut its 2030 population target to 100,000 and made Oxagon the priority.
